chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, who said:

He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was asked about Tawhid, and he said: 'Verily, God — Mighty and Majestic — knew that in the end of times there would be peoples who investigate deeply. So God the Exalted revealed
and the verses from Surah al-Hadid up to His words:
"and He is All-Knowing of what is in the chests"
So whoever seeks beyond that has perished.

key_terms.التوحيد: Tawhid — the doctrine of Divine Unity/Oneness; the foundational creedal principle in Islam
key_terms.رام وراء ذلك: Seeks beyond that — the fatal error of going beyond the revealed limits in theological speculation
key_terms.متعمقون: Those who investigate deeply/philosophize; referring to those who engage in speculative theology (kalam) beyond what revelation permits

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah reveal Surah Ikhlas and Surah al-Hadid according to Imam Zayn al-Abidin?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-'Abidin (peace be upon him), the 4th Imam, explained the divine wisdom behind the revelation of Surah al-Ikhlas and certain verses of Surah al-Hadid. He taught that Allah, in His foreknowledge, revealed these passages specifically to address those in later generations who would engage in deep metaphysical speculation about God's nature. The Imam drew a clear boundary: the revealed texts are sufficient guidance on Tawhid, and anyone who seeks to go beyond what is stated therein has gone astray and perished.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Aasim Bin Humeyd who said,

‘Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws was asked about the Tawheed (Oneness), so heasws said: ‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Knows that there would happen to be a people at the end of times who would be investigating in depth. So Allahazwj the Exalted Revealed
[112:1] Say: He Allah is One
, and the Verses from Surah Al-Hadeed (Chapter 57) up to His<sup>azwj</sup> Words
[57:6], and He is Aware of what is in the chests
. So whoever aims behind (any more than) that, so he is destroyed’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from ‘Asim ibn Hamiyd who has said the following.

“I asked Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) about the Oneness of Allah. The Imam replied, “Allah the Almighty, the Great, the Exalted knew that in the latter times there will be people who would investigate the issues very deeply in a hair splitting manner. Therefore, Allah, the Glorious, has revealed chapter one hundred twelve of the holy Quran that speak of the Oneness of Allah.

He has also revealed the verses of the chapter fifty seven of the holy Quran In the Name of God, the Beneficent, the Merciful All that is in the heavens and the earth speak of the glory of God. He is Majestic and All-wise [57:1]. To Him belongs the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes things to die. He has power over all things [57:2]. He is the First, the Last, the Manifest, and the Unseen and He knows all things [57:3]. It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established His Dominion over the Throne. He knows whatever enters into the earth, what comes out of it, what descends from the sky, and what ascends to it. He is with you wherever you may be and He is Well Aware of what you do [57:4]. To Him belong the heavens and the earth and to Him all things return [57:5]. He causes night to enter into day and day into night. He knows best what all hearts contain [57:6].
Whoever would accept any thing otherwise he is destroyed.”
